implementation_notes: Ruby has no channel primitive, and Queue is the closest: a thread-safe FIFO with push/pop (blocking) and SizedQueue(max) for a bounded one (push blocks when full - the channel's backpressure). It has no close, so termination is again a sentinel (a poison pill) put by the producer. For coroutine-style (non-blocking) channels, a Fiber-based bounded queue with push resuming a waiting pop (and vice versa) is the construction, which is the async-channel pattern; Ruby's SizedQueue already uses a Mutex internally and blocks the thread. Queue is condition-variable based, so it handles spurious wakeups correctly internally. SizedQueue is the right choice for a bounded hand-off between threads (it blocks the producer when full, giving backpressure); an unbounded Queue removes it. Because Ruby's Queue blocks a thread rather than suspending a coroutine, it cannot be used inside a Fiber without blocking the whole thread - a common confusion when mixing Fibers and SizedQueue.
idiom_name: SizedQueue(max) for a bounded thread-safe channel (backpressure); a sentinel value terminates; a Fiber-based async queue for non-blocking
code_sketch:
require 'thread'

# SizedQueue: a BOUNDED thread-safe channel - push blocks when full (backpressure).
q = SizedQueue.new(256)

Thread.new do
    jobs.each { |j| q.push(j) }   # blocks when full -> backpressure
    q.push(nil)                     # the 'close': a poison pill (Queue has no close)
end

loop do
    j = q.pop                        # blocks when empty (a channel's receive)
    break if j.nil?                  # the sentinel terminates the consumer
    handle(j)
end

# A plain Queue is UNBOUNDED - push never blocks, so there is no backpressure.
# For non-blocking (coroutine) hand-off, build a Fiber-based bounded queue
# where push resumes a waiting pop instead of blocking the thread.
pitfalls: Queue and SizedQueue have NO close: the producer must push a sentinel (poison pill) and the consumer must check it, or the consumer blocks forever.
SizedQueue blocks the pushing thread when full - correct for a thread hand-off, but it BLOCKS THE WHOLE THREAD if used inside a Fiber (it is not suspending).
A plain Queue (not SizedQueue) is unbounded: no backpressure, and a slow consumer grows it until OOM.
A Queue shared across processes is not a channel - it is an in-process thread primitive; use a pipe or a Socket for process hand-off.
Ruby's Queue is condition-variable based (correct with spurious wakeups) - a hand-rolled queue using a bare Mutex and a flag will not be.
alternative: SizedQueue(max) for a bounded thread hand-off; SizedQueue() unbounded as a simple work queue; a Fiber-based queue for non-blocking coroutine hand-off
